findings.description: Password hashing uses MD5, a broken and insecure algorithm. MD5 is susceptible to collision attacks, fast brute-force, and rainbow table attacks. This code reverts a previously merged security fix requiring bcrypt, leaving stored passwords vulnerable to compromise.

verify_password uses Python's == operator for hash comparison, which is not constant-time and may enable timing side-channel attacks. Use hmac.compare_digest or bcrypt.checkpw for secure verification.

This PR appears to conflict with an existing merged security fix that implemented bcrypt password hashing. The code intentionally reverts to MD5, creating a merge conflict and undoing a prior security hardening.
